sentences.text: Revenue compounded 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], while operating income grew faster at 9.9% [F146] and net income barely moved at 0.4% [F147].
The window is a growth-and-build story with two violent swings: operating margin fell 14.6pp in FY2021 to 15.5% [F20][D107], then jumped 23.5pp in FY2023 to 41.3% [F22][D177].
The FY2021 collapse came with a $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment in FY2020 and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity in FY2021 [P63][P68].
FY2023's margin spike reflected $1,729 million of non-qualifying hedge gains in NEER's net income [P30], a swing that reversed in FY2024 when NEER's results fell on unfavorable hedge activity [P36].
FPL remains the revenue base at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], contributing 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue rose $1,243 million on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
NEER's segment net income rose from $285 million in FY2022 [S26] to $2,975 million in FY2025 [S29], while FPL's reached $5,012 million [P23].
NEER's FY2025 increase came from new wind, solar and battery investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26][P13].
Operating income grew 10.7% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D237][D236], but operating costs grew 10.0% [D249], so there was no operating leverage.
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median [D300] but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [D299].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 from 23.2% [D224][D189], the main cost pressure, while stock-based compensation stayed at 0.7% [D223].
D&A expense increased $951 million in FY2025, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [P16].
Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% [F40][D248] even as operating margin edged up 0.3pp [D247], because other income (expense) was -$3,750 million [X64].
Corporate and Other's results fell $1,256 million, largely on about $1,002 million of unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][F32][D227], below the 1.95x window median [D319].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241] while investing outflow reached $23.9 billion [F72], so free cash flow was deeply negative and funded by $23.4 billion of debt issued [X90].
The shift from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million in FY2025 [P19].
Stock-based compensation is immaterial to cash at 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so conversion is driven by working capital and the capital programme, not equity pay.
Net debt widened for a seventh straight year to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231][R2], equal to 357.4% of revenue [D232].
That leverage ranks at the 0th percentile against three utilities peers, whose median net debt is 235.4% of revenue [D328][D329].
Liquidity is thin: cash of $2.8 billion [F96] against a 0.60x current ratio [F128], the window high but still below 1.0x [D305].
Free cash flow shortfalls were met with debt and $4.7 billion of dividends [D233][X82], while the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D251].
Net debt has risen every year of the window, from $34.3 billion in FY2018 to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231], the most persistent concern [R2].
The current ratio of 0.60x is below 1.0x [F128][R1], though it is the strongest level in the window [D305] and typical for a utility funding long-lived plant with short-term paper.
The FY2025 effective tax rate of -17.7% [D226] reflects NEER's clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million [P11], so the low rate is structural rather than an accounting error [R4].
FY2019 operating expenses were later restated to $14,257 million from $13,851 million [X18][R5], a data-quality caveat on that year's cost comparisons.
Watch whether operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median [D300]; a drop toward the 15.5% FY2021 low [D298] would signal hedge losses or cost pressure returning.
Watch net debt against the FY2025 level of $92.2 billion [D231]; further growth at the 15.7% FY2025 pace [D253] would extend the seven-year streak [R2].
Watch operating cash flow conversion against the 1.95x window median [D319]; a print below the 0.99x FY2018 low [D318] would flag working-capital strain.
